subject: Runway stress-test & cost levers for QBR (capacity, GPU econ, batching)
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Runway stress-test & cost levers for upcoming QBR

Team —

Ahead of the QBR (Nov 24 leadership slot) I want a concise, numbers-first summary we can hand to the execs. Focus areas:
- Current reserved vs. burst capacity (GPU pools) and month-over-month spend trend
- Utilization by route (interactive vs. background) and tail latency exposure
- Clear experiments we can run in the 72h window before the QBR that materially change runway (batching, cache tuning, short-term quantization toggles)

Please attach the updated model of runway impact (per-quarter cost delta) and a one-slide exec summary. I put a first-pass workbook in Drive and attached a working copy — update the white cells with your numbers.

Deliverables by EOD Mon (Nov 22):
1) One-slide exec summary (PDF)
2) Runway model workbook (xlsx) with scenario rows for: baseline, +batching, +cache, +reserved-commit
3) 30-min dry-run on Nov 23 at 10:00am PT to walk through the slide

Thanks — keep it tight, we only need high-confidence levers and downside risks.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: QBR_runway_summary_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 480KB)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Runway stress-test & cost levers for upcoming QBR

Lauren — thanks, brief update below (high level numbers; I attached simulated scenarios).

Baseline (last 30 days):
- GPU spend (hosted + reserved amortized): ~$1.21M / month
- Average GPU utilization across fleets: 62% (std dev 9%)
- Interactive routes (top 10 by volume): avg util 68%, 95th percentile latency 140ms token gen (p95 token latency)
- Background/batch jobs: avg util 47% but high opportunity to pack
- KV cache hit rate (production mix): 27% overall; customer-prefix hot routes hit ~45%

Levers & modeled impact (quarterly):
1) Aggressive batching for background workers (8x where safe): ~-$160k / quarter
2) Moderate batching on interactive routes (2–4x with adaptive latency guardrails): ~-$110k / quarter, increases p95 by ~10–25ms depending on request size
3) KV cache tuning + prefetch for predictable flows: increasing hit rate to 40% => ~-$95k / quarter
4) Short-term quantization on non-sensitive models (int8 for reranker variants): ~-$210k / quarter, requires validation for quality regressions
5) Increase reserved commits to avoid premium burst pricing: amortized net savings depends on utilization; modeled scenario shows $70–120k / quarter benefit at 75%+ utilization vs baseline with bursts

Notes on risk & ops:
- Canaries required for any change that touches interactive routes. Recommend a canary (1% traffic) + automated rollback on p95 increase >30ms or error rate >0.2%.
- Autoscaler: current min scale-down timer 60s — lengthening to 180s improves batching opportunities but increases idle GPU cost; modeling included in the workbook.
- Short window experiments: we can run the batching canary and KV prefetch trial in parallel; quantization needs a longer validation (per-model test suites).

I've attached the scenario CSV and a snapshot of the heatmap (for exec slide). I'll join the Nov 23 dry run and can present the tradeoffs; happy to pair with Hannah on the simulation details.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Infrastructure Economics
Redwood Inference

Attachment: batching-simulations.csv (data, 78KB)
Attachment: kv-cache-hitrates.png (image, 240KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Runway stress-test & cost levers for upcoming QBR

Quick notes from infra ops / experiments POV:

- Background: If we enable 8x effective packing for batch pipelines (windowed at 30s, opportunistic coalescing) the simulation Markus shared shows Q/Q savings of ~$160k. Ops impact: longer job wait times (median +26s), but customer-facing SLAs unaffected for background processing.

- Interactive routes: we can try adaptive batching with dynamic latency budgets; our telemetry shows that 2x–3x batching on medium-size prompts yields the majority of savings while keeping p95 within the 30ms guardrail. We'll implement an adaptive policy for the Nov 22 canary: start 2x, step to 4x if p95 < 120ms.

- Autoscale tuning: lengthening the min-ready window to 180s and enabling a small pool of warm nodes in us-west (n=6 gpus) during 12:00–18:00 PT reduced tail provisioning cost in sim by ~7%. Ops risk: increases idle amortized cost but unlocks batching.

Action items for the dry run:
1) Markus — bring the slide with the three scenarios (baseline, batching+cache, batching+cache+quant) and the run-rate savings.
2) Hannah — bring Ops runbook: canary configs + rollback thresholds + warm-node plan.
3) Lauren — have the exec summary slide and explicit ask for any one-off reserved commit approval if needed.

I'll prepare a short snippet to show live telemetry thresholds for canary gating.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Runway stress-test & cost levers for upcoming QBR

Thanks for the clear framing. A couple of executive asks to bake into the slide:

1) Customer impact statement — quantify how each lever affects SLAs or perceived latency for the top 5 customer accounts (good to have a 1-line impact per-account).
2) Downside scenarios — list worst-case rollback cost of each lever (time to restore baseline + any customer credits we might expect).
3) Ask for authority: if we need a one-off reserved commit for Dec–Feb to lock in capacity, what's the approval path and threshold (I want a dollar ask on the slide).

Also — we should loop in Brightline (ops contact Brad) for a sanity check on the interactive latency tradeoffs before we go to execs. I can do that outreach if you want.

Schedule: Nov 23 dry run at 10:00am PT confirmed on my calendar. Please upload the slide deck to the Drive link so I can validate the dollar ask and the downside language.

— Vivek
